scenario: [LTIM.2.5.1] / [IRET.19.5]: a clock tick never re-creates an activation, and an UNRELATED working-memory change does not clear refraction either. A now()-gated rule matures and fires once; then a fact the rule never matches is asserted and pumped, and the clock advances with the condition still true. The rule must not fire again. `formal/tla/refraction_readings.tla`'s `tick_reeval` stream: the literal clear-on-any-assert reading fires a second time here, the flag reading does not. Path: libds's per-fact one-shot, which survives the generation advance the unrelated assert causes (rete/engine.c); Mercury's refraction key with the synthetic tick excluded (ds.agenda.refraction_key) and the tick exempt from the forget (ds.engine.settle_fact_split).
rules_ds:
import calendar

schema Sensor scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

schema Other scope logical:
    v: Int key

rule after_5_s:
    Sensor where now() > calendar.time(1970, 1, 1, 0, 0, 5)
->
    log info "time passed"
